report.summary: All 12 boutique pods restarted/rescheduled within the same ~5s window immediately after node k3d-sre-lab-agent-1 was cordoned, consistent with a drain that evicted pods and forced them onto the remaining schedulable node k3d-sre-lab-server-0.
report.root_cause: Node k3d-sre-lab-agent-1 was cordoned (unschedulable taint added at 09:16:38Z, confirmed by NodeNotSchedulable event at 09:16:47Z), most likely as part of a maintenance/drain operation. This evicted the boutique pods resident on it, and the scheduler placed all of them onto k3d-sre-lab-server-0 simultaneously, producing the observed synchronized restart across otherwise-unrelated services. All services are now Ready with 0 restarts, confirming this was a one-time reschedule event rather than an ongoing application defect.
evidence: get_node_status: NodeNotSchedulable event on agent-1 at 2026-09-20T09:16:47Z
get_node_status: prior NodeSchedulable event on agent-1 at 2026-09-20T09:13:23Z, indicating a schedulable->cordoned flip consistent with a drain cycle
get_workload_status: all 12 boutique pods show start_time clustered between 09:16:40Z-09:16:45Z, all on node k3d-sre-lab-server-0
get_workload_status: every pod currently restart_count=0 and Ready=true, ruling out CrashLoopBackOff/ImagePullBackOff as the trigger
alternatives: Bad rollout/image change causing simultaneous CrashLoopBackOff (0.05): restart_count=0 on all pods and no unavailable replicas; 12 unrelated services with different images wouldn't crash-loop in lockstep from one rollout

Cluster-wide resource saturation causing evictions (0.05): get_node_status shows MemoryPressure=False/DiskPressure=False/PIDPressure=False on all nodes; no OOMKilled/eviction reasons in any pod container state

Network policy change causing probe failures and restarts (0.03): no CrashLoopBackOff or probe-failure reasons present; pattern of fresh pod names on a single new node matches reschedule, not in-place probe-failure restarts
Deliberate scale-down/up of multiple deployments (0.02): desired=1/ready=1 for all deployments with no scale-to-0 indication, and doesn't explain the coincident agent-1 cordon timestamp
report.impact: Brief simultaneous restart/reschedule of all 12 boutique microservices (adservice, cartservice, checkoutservice, currencyservice, emailservice, frontend, loadgenerator, paymentservice, productcatalogservice, recommendationservice, redis-cart, shippingservice) causing a short window of unavailability/latency during pod rescheduling; cluster has since stabilized with all pods Ready and 0 restarts.

remediation.action: Confirm intent of the drain/cordon on k3d-sre-lab-agent-1 and uncordon it if the maintenance is complete, to restore capacity and rebalance pods across nodes
remediation.rationale: The node was cordoned (likely for maintenance/drain); if that maintenance is finished, uncordoning restores it to the scheduling pool so future pod placement is spread across both agent nodes instead of concentrating everything on k3d-sre-lab-server-0, reducing blast radius of any future single-node incident

timeline.what: Node k3d-sre-lab-agent-1 event NodeSchedulable — node was schedulable at this point
Node k3d-sre-lab-agent-1 event NodeNotSchedulable fired, confirming the cordon took effect

All 12 boutique pods (adservice, cartservice, checkoutservice, currencyservice, emailservice, frontend, loadgenerator, paymentservice, productcatalogservice, recommendationservice, redis-cart, shippingservice) show fresh start_time within this ~5s window, all scheduled onto node k3d-sre-lab-server-0
get_workload_status shows every deployment Ready/Available with 0 restarts on any pod — cluster has stabilized post-reschedule

correlation.what_changed: Node k3d-sre-lab-agent-1 was cordoned (unschedulable taint added at 09:16:38Z, NodeNotSchedulable event at 09:16:47Z) — consistent with a drain operation — which forced every boutique pod that had been running on that node off it and onto k3d-sre-lab-server-0 simultaneously, producing the observed cluster-wide, same-moment pod restarts across unrelated services.
correlation.summary: The evidence points to a node-level event rather than any application defect: no pod shows CrashLoopBackOff, ImagePullBackOff, elevated restart_count, or error logs, and no rollout/image change is implicated. Instead, all boutique pods' start_times cluster tightly around 09:16:40-45Z immediately after node k3d-sre-lab-agent-1 was cordoned/drained (taint added 09:16:38Z, NodeNotSchedulable at 09:16:47Z). This is the standard signature of a node drain: pods that were resident on the cordoned node were evicted and rescheduled en masse onto the remaining schedulable node (k3d-sre-lab-server-0), which explains why 'multiple, unrelated' services all restarted at the same time despite each being individually healthy now.

hypotheses.cause: Node k3d-sre-lab-agent-1 was cordoned/drained around 09:16:38Z, evicting all pods that were scheduled on it, which were then simultaneously rescheduled onto k3d-sre-lab-server-0 (explaining the synchronized restart of unrelated pods)
supporting: get_node_status shows k3d-sre-lab-agent-1 tainted node.kubernetes.io/unschedulable:NoSchedule added 1m ago (2026-09-20T09:16:38Z)
NodeNotSchedulable event on agent-1 at 09:16:47Z, immediately preceding the pod restarts
All boutique pods show start_time clustered at 09:16:40-09:16:45Z, i.e. within seconds of the cordon event
All rescheduled pods landed on the same node, k3d-sre-lab-server-0, consistent with eviction-and-reschedule rather than independent crashes
Node also shows a prior NodeSchedulable at 09:13:23Z then re-cordoned at 09:16:38Z, consistent with a drain/maintenance cycle rather than steady-state
against: We did not directly confirm via events that the pods were previously running ON agent-1 before eviction (no pre-incident pod placement data available)
Cordoning alone (taint) does not evict running pods; an explicit drain/delete step would be required to force eviction, which we haven't directly observed

hypotheses.cause: A bad rollout/image change triggered near-simultaneous CrashLoopBackOff across services
supporting: Mass, correlated restart timing could superficially resemble a coordinated rollout
against: All pods currently show restart_count=0, not climbing restarts expected from CrashLoopBackOff
get_workload_status shows every deployment fully Ready/Available with no unavailable replicas
No rollout history was checked showing a new revision at that time, and the uniform restart across 12 unrelated services with different images makes a single bad rollout implausible

hypotheses.cause: Cluster-wide resource saturation (CPU/memory pressure) causing evictions on server-0
supporting: Multiple pods restarting at once could indicate node pressure evictions
against: get_node_status shows MemoryPressure=False, DiskPressure=False, PIDPressure=False on all nodes including server-0 and agent-1
No OOMKilled or eviction reasons reported in pod container states (all last_reason=null)

hypotheses.cause: Network policy or connectivity change caused pods to fail health checks and restart
supporting: Restarts occurring simultaneously across services could theoretically stem from a shared networking change
against: No NetworkPolicy data was gathered yet, but current pod states show 0 restarts and Ready=true with no CrashLoopBackOff/probe-failure reasons
Restart/reschedule pattern (new pod names, fresh start_times, same node) matches eviction/reschedule, not in-place restart due to failed probes

hypotheses.cause: Deliberate scale-down/scale-up (replicas set to 0 then back) of multiple deployments
supporting: Would also produce fresh pod start_times across many deployments
against: get_workload_status shows desired=1 and ready=1 for all deployments with no indication of a scale-to-0 event in rollout history
This would not explain the coincident agent-1 cordon/taint event at the same timestamp
